old_row.relationship: Confession parallel: David admits foolishness after the census
old_row.rationale: David confesses great sin, asks removal of his servant's wickedness or lawlessness, and acknowledges extreme folly in both accounts. Samuel explicitly places the confession after David's heart struck him following the count.

new_row.relationship: Confession parallel: David admits foolishness after the census
new_row.rationale: David confesses great sin, asks God to take away his wickedness or lawlessness, and acknowledges extreme folly in both accounts. Samuel explicitly places the confession after David's heart struck him following the count.

changes.reason: David asks concerning his own wickedness as God's servant; the former rationale could instead make David's servant the offender.

old_row.relationship: Same-chapter roster purpose: Kis's son Iramael within Levitical allocation
old_row.rationale: The source adds Iramael as Kis's son. The following summary identifies the continuing list as Levites by ancestral houses who received lots alongside Aaron's sons, explaining the function of this otherwise brief family entry.

new_row.relationship: Same-chapter roster purpose: Kis's son Iramael within Levitical allocation
new_row.rationale: The source adds Iramael as Kis's son. The following summary identifies the continuing list as Levites by ancestral houses who also received lots, as Aaron's sons did, explaining the function of this otherwise brief family entry.

changes.reason: The source compares the Levites' lots with Aaron's sons using as did; alongside could imply a joint allocation that the source does not explicitly state.
